posts.t:
Having a journal of any sort is very personal. I have made my journal public here first and foremost, because I do not trust myself to keep an accurate record privately of my learning. Secondly I want to climb to the top of the RTM ladder!

I envision that I will update this first post to form a table of contents, an organised linked record as opposed to a linear read through. I am imagining coming back to visit regularly over the 12 months time to see a post littered with links to nuggets of discoveries I have made and documented in this journal.

Let's begin.

H1/H4 - I noticed GJ had been compressing to a marked Support line now Resistance. M5 - I drop down as low as M5 to find price structure at this previous support line to find the pocket of potential supply. An FTR was found. Caution - Price has already visited this area. An FTB has been and gone. Trading to the right - Asian session sent price towards the FTR with a strong bullish candle. But price stalls, price consolidates and does not break higher. London Open is also unable to break higher, PA on the M30 chart I had been observing creates long upper wicks two times. I send my sell order to my broker.
LIKE

Thank you benhur.

Continuation: M5 - Price declines sharply, engulfing the lower time-frame support and forming a new FTR immediately after with momentum. Caution - Price bounces noticeably forming a V shape on this timeframe. I am always cautious about this type of approach. Trading to the right - Caution noted, price hasn't created new demand, nor is price reacting of 'fresh' demand on the HTFs I observe. Price actually stalls before the FTR and begins to curl over. I place a limit order to provide best value. I am filled and watch the HTF Price Action to justify holding the trade.
Great trading!

Thanks strudl.

Conclusion: TG1 & TG2 reached. Hindsight: This trade very quickly showed I could have doubled the trade reward by waiting longer. I can think of various tasks for my to-do list. This could be the catalyst to collect statistics on taking different type of trade exits. There is always a decision to be made at each stage of the trade. Entries. Active trade period. News events. Exits. Perhaps in this case I could have employed a trailing stop. Or waited for PA in the opposite direction. Sorry guys just thinking out loud here. Expectation vs Anticipation vs Doubt vs Cold Hard Statistics! <--- This is what I want to build. Sometimes I feel you can spend so much time trying to find that perfect entry and when you finally get it, it doesn't end there, your guard is a little down, and then you realise the tough battle to fight when it comes to exits. Maybe a little more. Maybe a little less.

H4 - I watched price find support @ 1.47. A bullish outside bar into a supply zone (marked with red line). Price did not progress higher in the Asian session. Caution - AU news to be wary of. Possible change in sentiment given the Price Action of a the bullish H4 candle at a reasonable spot on the chart for support to form. Trading to the right - My bias is short. The weekly chart tells me down. The daily chart tells me down. It is only a matter of safe stop placement. I execute a sell order prior to news, knowing that AUD headfakes are usually quite reliable to place stops behind recent supply/demand zones. Thinking ahead - There are some weekly targets a couple of hundred pips lower that I have my eyes on. I will watch price on the H4 and up charts for other exit opportunities.

WK/M30 - Price arrives at prior weekly resistance area. Let's assume there are willing buyers here. Once the S/R is hit we watch for price structure to confirm our bias. M30 shows that we have an engulf of the most recent FL. A good sign of things to come to put the odds in our favour. Caution - AU news to be wary of. Trading to the right - Bias is long based on proximity of weekly resistance, anticipating to become temporary support. What actually happened - As you can see I took the trade before news. Price action confirms this bias ahead of time. Stop was however placed safely below the LTF FTR. It is actually the 2nd time back as the news spike collects remaining buy orders.

Hatching plans on USDCHF. This was just triggered as I am typing this post.

M30 - Price is at Daily supply. Creating my short bias. An engulf of minor support levels. Diamond like pattern forming. Caution - Price hasn't engulfed the FTR currently holding price UP and news has used this FTR a third time to fill more buy orders. Approach to supply not pretty. My bias could be ill informed or a fakeout play still possible. Trading to the right - Trading the FTB to this FTR for science. Learn by doing.

Read The Market -Momentum is bearish as evidenced by the long bear candle to the left of the M30 chart. This creates the bias to find supply. -The FTR I have chosen held the most significance to my eyes. It aligned well with LTF FTR and price structure. -Asian session created the FTR but it was choppy coming out; London ran with it to create new lows in recent days. New York came back to fill more shorts and created a new low for the day. This was an opportunity I missed (first orange arrow) Caution -Time of the day. FTR is not fresh. Price has made a new high for the day, but I would not call it an engulf of the FTR having inspected it closer on M5. Trading to the right -I don't want to be buying at these levels so I am looking for sell opportunities based on my read. -Price develops tradeable price structure in my zone, in the direction I am anticipating. -I place one sell order, and then price gives a second opportunity to add with low risk.

I don't trade shares but I am assuming the stock markets play to the same patterns so I felt like drawing on some charts. Coming from Australia, I do hear often about the ASX 200 (Australia's Top 200 companies) from time to time and it appears to have been on quite the bull run for 2+ years now (5+ if you take the lowest swing low). I just wonder if the big boys have already taken their profits and are looking to unload the remainder during the second half of this year. Will be reading the headlines closely to see how this game is played. All I have heard from general punters the last year is how well their stocks are doing! Must be a sign the end is near I thought...

ASX 200 Monthly Maybe sell the market off for about 10%, instil some fear in the general public with sensationalistic headlines of "Billions lost" and continue on higher...
